paper_metadata.title: End-to-end resource analysis for quantum interior point methods and portfolio optimization

summary: This paper gives an end-to-end resource analysis of a gate-based quantum interior point method for portfolio optimization, not a hardware demonstration. For n=100 assets, it estimates about 8×10^6 logical qubits, 2×10^24 T-depth, and 7×10^29 T-count, with roughly 6×10^12 circuit repetitions overall; the authors conclude the approach is far from practical and that the classical portfolio problem is solvable in seconds on a laptop.

experiments.description: End-to-end quantum interior point method (QIPM) for second-order cone portfolio optimization, including numerical simulation of small portfolio instances and resource estimation for a fault-tolerant gate-based implementation.

algorithm.variant: Quantum interior point method for SOCP using a quantum linear system solver (QLSS) with discrete adiabatic evolution and tomography
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Terminate when duality gap µ < ϵ; in the implementation, iterations reduce µ by factor σ each step

hyperparameters.m: number of time epochs used to build covariance factor M; set to 2n in numerical experiments
hyperparameters.epsilon_tsp: state-preparation error in tomography sign-estimation step

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Initialize on the self-dual central path at (x,y,τ,θ,s,κ)=(e,0,1,1,e,1); tomography precision is adapted by starting at ξ=1/2 and halving until the point remains in the central-path neighborhood

optimizer_settings.step_size: chosen so duality gap shrinks by factor σ each iteration

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Portfolio optimization is reduced to an SOCP with variables x=(w,ϕ,ρ,t,η) and self-dual embedding variables (τ,θ,κ); the Newton linear system is solved quantumly. Classical data are loaded via QRAM-based block-encoding and state preparation.
problem_formulation.objective_function: min_w -u_hat^T w + q*sqrt(w^T Σ w) subject to 1^T w = 1, |w-w_bar| <= zeta, w >= 0; after SOCP reformulation, objective is c^T x with c=[-u_hat;0;0;q;0]
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: SOCP reformulation with auxiliary variables t, η, ϕ, ρ; self-dual embedding for initialization; feasibility maintained either approximately (II-QIPM) or via null-space basis (IF-QIPM variants)
problem_formulation.num_ancilla_qubits: QRAM ancillas and tomography ancillas are used; exact total ancilla count not separately reported

problem_instance.description: Portfolio optimization on randomly sampled stocks from the Dow Jones U.S. Total Stock Market Index (DWCF), using historical return data to build mean returns and covariance factor M
problem_instance.dataset_name: Dow Jones U.S. Total Stock Market Index (DWCF)

dataset_specification.description: Historical stock returns; example uses first m=60 days for n=30; scaling studies use m=2n days

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Compute average return vector u_hat and matrix M from return deviations so that M^T M = Σ; choose q=1, zeta=0.05*1, and current portfolio w_bar proportional to market capitalization
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Simulate the full QIPM classically on many random portfolio instances; 128 random samples per n for scaling plots; adaptive tomography precision; compare II-QIPM, IF-QIPM, and IF-QIPM-QR; resource estimates reported for n=100 at target duality gap 1e-7

error_correction.code_type: fault-tolerant logical-level analysis only; no specific code

noise_model.error_mitigation_method: none; resource analysis assumes fault-tolerant logical circuits and classical simulation is used only for numerical study of parameters

implementation_details.classical_solver: Classical exact linear solver used only inside numerical simulation of the quantum subroutine; ECOS and Gaussian elimination discussed as classical baselines
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Construct SOCP from portfolio optimization; compute M, A, b, c; precondition Newton matrix by row normalization; classically compute block-encoding angles and gate decompositions; optionally compute null-space basis by inspection or QR decomposition for feasible variants
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Tomography reconstructs classical estimate of Newton step; update interior-point iterate classically; return x/τ as portfolio weights

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: duality gap decreases exponentially with iterations; tomography precision initially decreases then plateaus

speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical interior point methods / classical linear system solvers
speedup_claims.conditions: gate-based fault-tolerant implementation of QIPM for portfolio optimization
speedup_claims.caveats: Paper explicitly concludes that resource counts are prohibitively large and do not provide significant evidence for an asymptotic polynomial quantum speedup; tomography and block-encoding overheads dominate.

speedup_claims.factor: up to O(min(xi^2*kappa_F, xi^2*L^2/kappa_F)) advantage in linear-system subroutine
speedup_claims.conditions: comparing QLSS + tomography against classical linear-system solvers
speedup_claims.caveats: Advantage is limited, depends on condition number and precision, and may vanish when kappa_F is too large or too small.

speedup_claims.conditions: if kappa_F proportional to n and xi = O(1)
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper says this is only a hypothetical asymptotic scenario; numerical results do not support xi = O(1) and practical constants are very large.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Full QIPM leading-order runtime scales as O(kappa_F * L * sqrt(r) * xi^-2 * log(1/epsilon) * log(L) * log(kappa_F * L^(14/27) * xi^-1)); asymptotically, the linear-system subroutine is O(kappa_F * xi^-2) up to logs
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Classical IPM with Gaussian elimination is O(n^3.5) for the portfolio formulation; classical linear-system solvers also include randomized Kaczmarz O(L*kappa_F^2*log(xi^-1))
complexity_analysis.constant_factor_quantum: Very large; paper reports QLSS prefactor around 4e7 in the linear-system comparison and 1.31*2305 in the QLSS estimate
complexity_analysis.constant_factor_classical: Gaussian elimination prefactor about 1/3 in the linear-system comparison; randomized Kaczmarz prefactor about 8
complexity_analysis.total_operations_quantum: About 6e12 circuit repetitions for n=100 when including tomography and IPM iterations; about 3e8 block-encoding/state-preparation queries per QLSS circuit
complexity_analysis.total_operations_classical: PO problem solvable in seconds on a laptop for n=100; classical IPM scaling O(n^3.5)
complexity_analysis.wall_clock_quantum: Even with 4GHz QRAM, estimated on the order of ten thousand years for the full n=100 PO instance
complexity_analysis.wall_clock_classical: Seconds on a laptop for n=100

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not established; paper reports no practical crossover and only analyzes n up to 120, with a concrete resource estimate at n=100.
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: The paper estimates 8e6 logical qubits, 2e24 T-depth, and 7e29 T-count for n=100, plus about 6e12 circuit repetitions overall; even with 4 GHz QRAM the authors estimate roughly ten thousand years.
limiting_factors: Very large tomography overhead scaling as 1/xi^2
Large QLSS constant factors and condition number kappa_F
About 8e3 IPM iterations at n=100, epsilon=1e-7
Classical PO instance is solvable in seconds on a laptop at n=100

notes: hardware.type is not specified because the paper is a resource-analysis study, not a hardware execution paper

speedup_order inferred as none_proven because the paper explicitly states the numerical results do not provide significant evidence for an asymptotic polynomial quantum speedup and emphasize practical infeasibility
num_qubits and circuit-depth values are taken from the paper's resource tables and n=100 estimate
The paper is an end-to-end resource analysis, not a hardware benchmark.
Authors explicitly state the resource counts are prohibitively large and do not provide evidence for practical quantum advantage.
